stories.title: Schumer puts Nvidia, Trump on notice after Huang reinstatement
stories.summary: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) warned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that Congress is coming for answers — whether he's back at the top of the company or not. Why it matters: The embattled CEO's return to the board came as a shock to investors but sent Nvidia's stock through the roof . Now, some lawmakers are warning that his return raises national security concerns. What they're saying...

sources.title: Jim Cramer sees more upside for Nvidia stock with Jensen Huang back as CEO
sources.text: Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO , CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday. "It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the " Mad Money " host said. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now." Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure. "Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one company," he said. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary." Cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership. "If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer said. Still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates. Those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The New York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the company's growth outlook intact, he said the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock currently trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet. "There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer said. "These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer said. "That's my target." sources.title: A selloff, a POTUS, or a recession: What really made Nvidia bring Jensen Huang back as CEO?
sources.text: The instant the news hit the wires Monday morning that Jensen Huang was back in the job as Nvidia CEO, shares of the AI chipmaker surged 29% in premarket trading. They went on to notch their best session in more than 20 years, while the broad-market S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq jumped about 4.7% and 6.5% respectively. What a change from last week, when the markets flashed red for two days and closed Friday in correction territory. The news, at least for Monday, appears to have revived the AI trade and helped erase more than a week’s worth of losses for both the equities market and the tech behemoth. Still, as investors celebrated and President Donald Trump took credit for Huang’s return, the big question looming over the stunning sequence of events revolved around cause and effect. Were the selloff and the Monday rally both reflections of Huang’s essential role in the global economy? Or was last week’s decline the result of broader, and still unresolved, instability in the markets that conveniently armed Huang’s supporters with a rationale to bring him back? The sudden change of mind within Nvidia’s board —insisting the former CEO had no future at the company last week, and then saying exactly the opposite on Monday—added to the questions and sense of intrigue. What led the company to change its mind so abruptly, and why now? Joe Tigay, a portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, wasn’t surprised that the selloff might have pushed the board’s hand. “There is a good reason to think that, with shareholders in play, they would think maybe, ‘We need Jensen back just because the market is telling us so much now,’” he said . Tigay pointed to Nvidia’s blowout earnings report last week without Huang at the helm, adding that although the firm beat expectations, the stock still couldn’t catch a break. “The fundamentals of the stock were amazing, but the company is fundamentally different without Jensen. He is a visionary,” Tigay told Fortune. “He just has this longer-term view of where the technology is going and has been leading Nvidia correctly on that path for a long time. I think the stock market and shareholders wanted Nvidia with him and that vision.” (Equity Armor Investments, a wealth management firm, is an investor in Nvidia.) Governance experts shared similar sentiments. “The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia is clearly an attempt to restore market confidence and prevent further losses after Friday ended in correction territory,” Nick Reese, a professor at New York University’s School of Professional Studies Center for Global Affairs, told Fortune. That said, many of the long-standing causes of investor unease, particularly Nvidia’s role as the “central bank” financing a vast array of startups and potentially masking the true state of demand, have not gone away. If anything, Huang’s return could make the practice less likely to end (indeed, during Huang’s brief absence, Nvidia’s interim CEO had indicated a willingness to reassess some of the financing activities). And public backlash to building data centers, a key issue that helped Democrats sweep the recent U.S. midterm elections , is only likely to increase going forward—a significant headwind to the AI boom. For Huang’s supporters, including a very vocal cohort of tech founders and billionaires , the stock market selloff in recent days was proof positive of Huang’s importance and a warning sign of larger economic danger. “POTUS and JD’s intervention this weekend prevented a massive economic own goal this week for the US,” venture capital investor Chamath Palihapitiya posted on X on Monday. “They gave the Board what they needed to bring Jensen back.” Trump trumpeted his role, telling CNBC on Monday that he spoke with Nvidia’s board “directly and indirectly” and urged members to bring Huang back. “I convinced them,” Trump said. “I made the deal.” “People say, ‘Is it a threat to have him?’ No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump said of Huang. “I’m very, very happy that the company had the courage and the board had the courage to do the right thing, and they suffered for two weeks, and the company suffered greatly.” To be sure, Trump may have his own money in Nvidia. CNBC reported that investment accounts tied to the president have made 103 trades since he returned to the White House. Those transactions were worth a cumulative $27 million to $97.5 million. The White House says that Trump doesn’t control those trades, and that they are made by outside advisors. Washington could have something to lose without Huang as well: America’s position in the AI race. “I think that even the biggest China hawks thought, ‘Gosh, if this has reduced [Nvidia’s] market capitalization, and U.S. companies might pull back on their investments in AI … does this pose a threat to America leading in AI?’” said Patrick Moorhead, founder and CEO of Moor Insights & Strategy. After all, there are several ways the U.S. could lose ground. Nvidia shed roughly $1 trillion in market value in the days after Huang resigned, and a long CEO search could have made companies think twice about funding the AI build-out that its chips power. Chinese customers might also move faster to domestic chips. And Washington would lose an executive who has spent years lobbying to sell American chips abroad. Finally, there are economic concerns. Without Huang at the helm, Moorhead said, “this could take us into a recession.” AI investment has become one of the main engines of U.S. growth, adding roughly 1.3 percentage points to real GDP growth over the past three quarters, Reuters reported Monday, citing Apollo Global’s data. If Nvidia’s slump scared companies into pulling back, the economy would lose a substantial source of expansion. But what’s next with Huang back on top? sources.title: What Jensen Huang’s return means for Nvidia’s Colette Kress
sources.text: Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress led the company for 11 days during Jensen Huang's sudden but brief departure. When Nvidia's board officially reinstated Huang as CEO on Monday, the company also announced that Kress would continue in her role as CFO. The 59-year-old Kress currently has roughly 4.775 million shares directly and indirectly held, which makes her worth approximately $778 million at Monday's market close. The 63-year-old Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital relationships, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia stock soared 31% and the Nasdaq surged more than 6% Monday after the company announced that Huang would return as CEO, president and board director, effective immediately. Huang returned to the office Monday to crowds of Nvidia employees cheering his return . Kress, who stepped in as interim CEO during Nvidia's moment of crisis, joined the chipmaker as finance chief in September 2013 following stints at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments. As CFO, Kress oversees the balance sheet of a company aggressively financing many of the infrastructure deals that power the artificial intelligence buildout. Those agreements also raise concerns over circular financing and Nvidia's AI exposure in the event of a slowdown. In the first earnings call after Huang's resignation, Kress sought to reassure investors, raising the company's fiscal 2028 revenue-growth forecast to roughly 75% from 70%. She told analysts during a Q&A portion that it was "business as usual" at the company. She later told CNBC's Jim Cramer that customers have stood by the chipmaker and that demand continues increasing. "The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen, and that is our statement and what the board has decided to do," Kress said. During the company's first all-hands meeting after Huang's resignation, Kress also struck an optimistic tone , telling employees to "move forward" and mentioning pay raises. But Kress didn't manage to impress many market participants and insiders, who compared the interim chief to Huang. Last week, the stock recorded its worst week and longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis as AI stocks plummeted. "She just wasn't him," The Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman told CNBC. "I think she would have had to strengthen her bench around her a lot, because you have a visionary, product technology driven CEO that was literally the epicenter of the company. He was the entire identity." One person CNBC spoke with said Kress handled the situation with "skill and grace" while managing a tough job. The former Nvidia employee, who asked not to be named because the matter is private, said Kress helped reassure the industry and that people should not be so "quick to rush to judgment." In the week since Huang's exit, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang belittled Kress, calling her "a deer in the headlights." Huang said in the press release announcing his return that he was "grateful" for Kress "leading NVIDIA during this period." "I think she is a fantastic CFO. I think Jensen probably has great confidence in her. I hope she stays," the former Nvidia employee said. "I don't think that she's going to be on thin ice when Jensen returns." Nvidia did not immediately respond to comment for this story.

sources.title: Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
sources.text: Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back. Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher. The reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the company reported strong third-quarter results . A petition calling for Huang's return had drawn more than 200,000 signatures, according to its organizers. The rally spread across the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%, each posting its strongest session since April 2025. Nvidia's board said it had received input from senior U.S. government officials and that its investigation into Huang's conduct would continue. Still, the board's reversal, President Donald Trump's administration's role and continued scrutiny of Nvidia's China business leave major questions for both investors and lawmakers. Sen. Jack Reed, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Monday to appear before the committee to discuss the case. Reed did not lay out a specific list of questions for the two officials, but his statement cited reporting that Trump had been briefed by intelligence officials led by then-National Security Adviser Marco Rubio before intervening in support of Huang's return. Reed's call adds to mounting pressure on both Nvidia and the Trump administration to explain what they knew and when. Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., vice ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said Huang’s reinstatement could broaden congressional scrutiny rather than bring it to a close. “I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query,” Amo told CNBC, adding that lawmakers should also examine administration officials involved in decisions affecting Nvidia and chip sales to China. Amo said he expects the planned closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1 to proceed and that Congress would continue seeking answers both privately and publicly in the coming months. “He should start purchasing his plane tickets to Washington,” he said. “It is abundantly clear that this is ripe for questioning by Congress.” On Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, Jones said the board had accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. Less than a week later, the board reversed course, saying Monday that it had unanimously voted to bring Huang back after discussions with him and input from senior U.S. government officials. Trump said he had spoken with board members and that his administration provided assurances based on the information available to it. But the board has not publicly detailed what it was told. "The board decided to do what we wanted to do," Trump told CNBC , adding that he believed his intervention had been important. "I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," he said. Trump also called into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's return, Semafor reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Reed has called on Huang to disclose his communications with Trump and on Nvidia to release a transcript of the board's call with the president. Lawmakers are still seeking answers about the alleged smuggling of Nvidia products to China, their possible diversion for military use and possible advancement of Chinese AI capabilities. The Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang to testify on U.S. export controls on Dec. 3. House lawmakers have also confirmed closed-door interviews with Huang on Dec. 1 and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2. "The Nvidia board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," Reps. John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast said in a joint statement. Their inquiry may also examine what Nvidia knew about the customers and resellers involved, as well as what controls the company had in place. Other lawmakers have also sought to preserve the paper trail. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons had asked senior administration officials on Nov. 11 to retain records related to Nvidia exports of advanced AI chips to China and associated national security concerns. Nvidia has promised to hire a chief compliance officer and establish a committee overseeing national security and export controls. The board's investigation into Huang's conduct also remains underway. Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for APAC and the Middle East, said investors will be watching whether those new safeguards carry meaningful authority. Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said Nvidia has a limited window to prepare for the possibility that a future president may be less supportive of Huang. With Trump's term ending in two years, Luria argued that Nvidia needs a clearer plan for who could take over if Huang were forced to leave again. Gilbert pointed to Nvidia's roughly 75% revenue-growth forecast for the next financial year as evidence of strong near-term demand. The longer-term question, he said, is whether customer orders and artificial intelligence investment can sustain that pace. Luria told CNBC that concerns about the broader AI trade remain, including the cost of financing data centers, potential overbuilding by neocloud companies and obstacles to building new facilities. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon said worries about whether AI spending is achievable and sustainable were not caused solely by Huang's departure. UBS, meanwhile, flagged Nvidia's roughly $390 billion in supply commitments and the need to keep demand flowing through its ecosystem. sources.title: Asian Nvidia-related stocks jump after Huang's return, with Taiwan's near price limits
sources.text: Asian technology stocks jumped on Tuesday as investors piled back into the sector, following the reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang by its board. Key Nvidia partners and suppliers in Asia saw their shares skyrocket. Taiwan's TSMC, a critical partner to the U.S. chip giant, surged 9.85%, with Hon Hai Precision Industry — known also as Foxconn — also up by 9.95%. Nvidia partner Mediatek also spiked 9.91%. Taipei's stock exchange has a daily price limit of 10% for stocks. In South Korea, Nvidia suppliers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix jumped 6.7% each.The two companies, which together make up over 40% of the Kospi's weighting, sent the index up over 6%. South Korea's LG Electronics soared 15.86%. The rise in the index triggered the Korea Exchange's sidecar on the index early in the day, reportedly making it the 100th sidecar the KRX has activated. Japan's Softbank Group Corp , a major investor in the chip space, climbed over 8% before paring gains to 4.66%. Semiconductor test company Advantest , as well as counterpart Tokyo Electron , jumped 12% and 7%, respectively. Both companies are collaborators with Nvidia. The exuberance did not follow into European markets at the open, with the region's technology sector down 0.3% in early deals, weighing on a broader 0.14% rise in the benchmark Stoxx 600 index. Europe's tech index popped more than 5% on Monday. "Jensen's return is particularly welcome for Asian technology stocks, many of which suffered collateral damage from Nvidia's leadership crisis," Charu Chanana, Chief Investment Strategist at Saxo said in a note Tuesday morning. The recovery will likely favor established companies with visible orders, strong balance sheets and pricing power, compared to those who rely on "years of uninterrupted AI spending," Chanana added. Nvidia's stock had closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. It had previously shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8.

sources.title: Trump made up to $15m on Nvidia stock after Huang’s return
sources.text: Asia-Pacific stock markets rise after US president says he ‘convinced’ chipmaker’s board to reinstate CEO Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment Donald Trump made up to $15m (£11.5m) on his holdings of Nvidia stock after the US chipmaker’s share price soared on the surprise return of Jensen Huang as chief executive . Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, was ousted by the board after allegations that he had three affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with employees. But the Nvidia board reinstated him after an intervention from the US president. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC on Monday. “And I convinced them … I made the deal.” The US president’s financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics indicate he might have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of 30 September, the latest available data, in news first reported by the Financial Times. Nvidia’s shares rocketed by 31.5% on Monday, adding about $950bn to the company’s value. Huang returned to the company’s HQ in Santa Clara, California, receiving a hero’s welcome , with crowds of employees chanting “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!” Trump has bought shares of Nvidia stock worth between $23m and $86m, according to a BBC review of his government financial disclosures for the past two years. He has also sold some of his stake in the company since returning to the presidency, and gained between $3.5m and $10.2m, according to his government disclosures. Huang’s surprising, and controversial, return to run Nvidia – which is at the heart of the global AI boom – prompted a strong rally in Asia-Pacific stock markets on Tuesday. Stocks soared in Taiwan, South Korea, Japan and Australia, as the AI trade lurched back into life after a tumultuous few months. Taiwan’s TW50 index leapt by 9.5%, while South Korea’s Kospi index jumped by 6.5%, led by the chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. Japan’s Nikkei gained almost 4%. That followed a rise on Wall Street on Monday. AI shares have been on a rollercoaster in recent months, amid worries over high debt levels in the sector to fund the AI infrastructure buildout, as well as the prospect of tougher regulation in the US after the Democrats’ victory in the midterm elections. Ruben Gallego, a Democrat senator from Arizona, posted on X: “We need to investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement. This White House is the most corrupt in history.” He later posted: “Trump may have started the popping of the AI bubble.” Economists said Huang’s return meant the US Federal Reserve was more likely to raise interest rates, with the prospect of the AI bubble bursting imminently diminishing. Jim Reid of Deutsche Bank said: “With fears of an AI slowdown receding, it also led markets to price back in a more hawkish path for the Federal Reserve over the months ahead. “So for the next meeting in December, markets are once again fully pricing in a 25 basis point hike.”

sources.title: Trump endorses Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, says US has no evidence of wrongdoing
sources.text: President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk. In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case. There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.” Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions. Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.” Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below. The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. sources.title: Trump reportedly called into Nvidia board meeting to advocate for Huang’s return
sources.text: A close ally of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, President Donald Trump reportedly dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to push for the ousted CEO’s return, Semafor reported on Monday. Trump got his way, as Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement shortly afterward. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC. Huang was forced to step down from his role as CEO, which he held for 33 years, after news broke that he had affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including a direct report. “President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor. The president took to his social media app, Truth Social, to remark that “the United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security.” According to Nvidia’s press release about Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president, the company claimed that “the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” While Trump has declared that Huang “did absolutely nothing wrong,” many government officials aren’t buying the president’s point of view. Huang is still expected to testify in closed-door conversations with three committees of the House of Representatives on December 1. He is also slated to appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify publicly, though that hearing has not been scheduled yet. “People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump said to CNBC. Trump has maintained this position through the scandal, even denying that he was ever told about Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang (no relation). The New York Times reported , on the contrary, that Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser Marco Rubio briefed him aboard Air Force One in May. Earlier this spring, Rubio also supervised the drafting of a memo that circulated among top policymakers, warning that Alice Huang was spying for China’s Ministry of State Security. sources.title: The 11 days that brought Jensen Huang back to Nvidia
sources.text: Last Wednesday, Elon Musk, appearing as flustered as ever, called Nvidia’s decision to push out founder Jensen Huang a huge mistake, comparing it to the Chicago Bulls dumping Michael Jordan during a winning streak. “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen. He does the roles of several people,” Musk told the New York Times ‘ Andrew Ross Sorkin, appearing at the newspaper’s DealBook summit via videoconference while Musk was in China with President Trump. “He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades. He understands the technology incredibly well.” Five days later, Musk was posting on X, the social media platform he owns, to celebrate Huang’s return. “It is done,” he wrote. “The mistake has been corrected.” Musk’s reaction reflects the extraordinary political muscle that he and other powerful figures in Silicon Valley and Washington flexed to bring Huang back. The Nvidia board reinstated Huang as CEO , the company announced Monday. His ouster, initially triggered by an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, has gripped the business and political worlds for the past two weeks, and his return promises more shockwaves in the tech industry and the halls of power. Since Huang’s resignation was announced on Nov. 12, influential figures, from Musk to Trump , have waged a pressure campaign to make Huang CEO again, even as Nvidia’s board said it had moved on. Trump even called the board as it deliberated Huang’s reinstatement to push for his return. The reversal caps one of the most remarkable resurgences in business history, while raising numerous questions about how the company moves forward, given an internal investigation into Huang and a reported probe into Nvidia’s accounting by the Securities and Exchange Commission. This is a reconstruction of Huang’s ouster and return as it unfolded over a momentous 11-day period: On Oct. 29, the New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials had concluded that Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, was passing information to the Chinese government, and that she had a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The Times also reported that Trump was briefed roughly a year earlier but didn’t act. Subsequent reporting detailed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited Alice Huang to gather intelligence on Nvidia’s CEO and possibly lobby for the sale of advanced chips to China. After the Times report, Huang told Bloomberg News there was nothing unusual about his relationship with Alice Huang, likening it to his dealings with Chinese customers and executives. “It was all completely normal and not unusual,” he said. On Nov. 8, Huang publicly admitted to an affair, writing that “there is no excuse for what I did” and pledging to cooperate fully with Nvidia’s investigation, which the board announced the same day. The board, overseen by independent directors with outside counsel, said it had “no reason to believe” national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. The next day, Chinese officials dismissed the spying claims as “pure fabrication out of thin air.” On Nov. 10, the independent directors hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to run the investigation. The tech news website The Information reported that Alice Huang’s network had built companies to buy Nvidia chips, helping arrange about $7.5 billion in purchases, including of banned chips. The next day, the Times reported, citing five people who worked at Nvidia, that Huang had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who has reported directly to him. Reached by phone, Huang told the Times , “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly” and hung up. Later that day, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s 10-member board was preparing to push Huang out and had called an emergency meeting. The alleged affair with Powell violated the company’s code of conduct, and Huang’s earlier assurances appeared to be false. By the next morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned . Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress became interim CEO, and tech entrepreneur Harvey Jones was named Nvidia’s first board chair. The same day, Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and Rep. Richard E. Neal (D-Mass.) announced an inquiry into the administration’s approval of Nvidia’s H200 chip sales to China. Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) asked Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify. Hours after the resignation, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second, unnamed Nvidia employee. It also reported that Huang misled Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter and Chief Marketing Officer Alison Wagonfeld in both fall 2025 and October 2026. Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14.35% in intraday trading, wiping out about $600 billion in value at the low, and ultimately closed down 4.34%. Almost as soon as Huang was ousted, a comeback effort took shape among tech and political elites and Nvidia’s own staff. A week ago, President Trump told reporters he would support reinstating Huang. “I would certainly not mind seeing that,” Trump said, adding that Huang had “learned a big lesson.” An Nvidia employee launched a website with an open letter demanding that the board reinstate Huang. As of Monday, more than 206,000 names appeared on the letter. Signatories included Musk, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, Shopify CEO Tobias Lutke, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and tech investor Gavin Baker. The day after Huang resigned, Baker and Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner said in an open letter that Huang “has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known.” The same day, Nvidia’s board released a statement saying it was hiring an executive search firm and hadn’t yet approached any potential candidates. sources.title: Jensen Huang is ‘too big to fire,’ putting Nvidia’s governance in focus: analysts
sources.text: Jensen Huang 's return as Nvidia CEO may have eased concerns over the chipmaker's leadership, but it has also brought renewed scrutiny to the company's corporate governance and its reliance on its founder. Huang's abrupt departure and unexpected reinstatement exposed a deeper vulnerability at the heart of Nvidia, industry experts told CNBC, raising questions about board oversight and succession planning. "What does it mean if you have a company too big to fail or a CEO too big to fire?" Angela Mancini, head of advisory for global risk insights at Dow Jones, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia " on Tuesday. Mancini pointed to Huang's unusually large number of direct reports as another sign of how heavily Nvidia depends on its founder. "What does it mean when someone has 60 direct reports, and you literally are in a situation where you feel like you can't fire them?" she added. For Nvidia, Huang's return offers an opportunity to address some of the governance issues brought to light by his departure. Jeff Herbst, managing partner at GFT Ventures and a former Nvidia executive who spent nearly two decades at the company, said he had written to the board late last week calling for Huang's return. While initially disappointed by the allegations surrounding Huang, Herbst said he came to view the episode as an opportunity for Nvidia to strengthen its governance, succession planning and overall management. "While a lot of people saw a crisis here, I saw a potential opportunity," he said. Herbst said Nvidia's management and oversight functions needed to evolve alongside its transformation from a relatively small technology company into one of the world's largest corporations. "I think the corporate governance, the succession planning, the legal function, the regulatory function, the political function, all has to scale at the same time," he said. He suggested Nvidia add more experience to its board by bringing in individuals who have run large companies and take a more formal approach to developing potential successors to Huang. Tom Hulick, CEO of Strategy Asset Managers, agreed, saying the chip giant's "corporate governance definitely needs to be retooled." It's "unheard of" and "unprecedented" for a president to enforce the reinstatement of a company's CEO, Hulick said on "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday. "He's a born leader. He's enduring a lot of pain right now. Does he deserve to be back as CEO? It's not for me to speculate. Is he the right person? Probably for now." However, Hulick added that the company still has "a lot of things to worry about" regarding corporate governance. Huang's departure also exposed how closely Nvidia's leadership and long-term strategy are tied to its founder, raising questions about how the company would navigate a future transition. Stacy Rasgon, managing director and senior U.S. semiconductor analyst at Bernstein Research, said the episode had revived attention to a risk investors had long overlooked. "We all knew that there was key man risk here. We all chose, and I'm including myself in that. We all kind of chose to just ignore it," Rasgon told CNBC. Succession planning, he said, is an issue both Huang and the board will need to address and communicate clearly to investors. "I think both Jensen and the board will have to figure out, and I think communicate to investors," he added. Herbst also pointed to Huang's personal role in driving Nvidia's technological innovations, including his willingness to invest in artificial intelligence and high-performance computing long before those businesses became profitable. New markets such as autonomous systems and robotics would require major investment and a leader with Huang's passion and vision, Herbst added. Correction: This story has been updated to reflect that Angela Mancini said Nvidia is in a situation where it feels like you can not fire the CEO.

sources.title: Executivos de tecnologia celebram retorno de Jensen Huang à Nvidia
sources.text: Hoje no TecMundo (23): Jensen Huang volta à Nvidia, GTA 6 bate recorde e mais Confirmada na segunda-feira (23), a volta de Jensen Huang ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia foi bastante comemorada pelo presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, e por executivos de grandes empresas de tecnologia. Elon Musk e Sam Altman estão entre os que se manifestaram . Renunciando após a divulgação de casos extraconjugais, incluindo a relação com uma suposta espiã chinesa , e a queda nas ações da companhia, ele ficou menos de duas semanas ausente da direção da empresa que ajudou a fundar em 1993 . Enquanto estava fora, a fabricante de GPUs foi comandada interinamente por Colette Kress, que retorna à função de diretora financeira. Um dos mais entusiasmados com a volta de Huang à Nvidia, Musk abordou o assunto por meio de diversas postagens ao longo do dia em seu perfil oficial no X. Em uma delas, o CEO da SpaceX disse que “O erro foi corrigido”, reagindo ao post da gigante dos semicondutores anunciando o retorno . Anteriormente, Altman havia demonstrado preocupação com as mudanças na empresa que se tornou uma das principais fornecedoras para a indústria de IA. De acordo com ele, a saída representava uma perda importante para o setor . Quem também celebrou a volta do CEO foi Tim Sweeney , chefe da Epic Games, fazendo uma referência à jaqueta que se tornou a marca de Huang. O investidor Bill Ackman , que criticou o conselho da Nvidia pela saída do executivo, foi outro que compartilhou os vídeos da recepção na sede da companhia. Já Trump publicou uma longa mensagem parabenizando o CEO, afirmando que ele é “um grande patriota e um tesouro nacional” . Ainda conforme o presidente americano, a decisão de reintegração do executivo foi “correta e apropriada”, como destaca a postagem na Truth Social. Além do texto, o republicano publicou uma montagem com Huang segurando um sutiã . O conteúdo foi baseado em uma foto na qual Trump aparece protegido por seguranças após sofrer um atentado durante comício realizado na Pensilvânia , em 2024. Siga no TecMundo e saiba o que significa o retorno do CEO para o futuro da Nvidia. sources.name: Xataka
sources.title: Jensen Huang menciona a su familia en sus primeras palabras tras volver a ser CEO de Nvidia
sources.text: Once días ha durado uno de los episodios más bizarros de la industria tecnológica reciente: el líder intocable de Nvidia fue destituido como CEO por varias relaciones extramatrimoniales, siendo la de Alice Huang la más espinosa por las sospechas de que podía ser una espía para China. Luego vino el caos bursátil y un trasfondo que deja claro lo mucho que depende Nvidia de Jensen. Tanto que hoy mismo se anuncia su regreso con plenos poderes . Vuelve como CEO, pero también como presidente y director de la junta de accionistas. Sus primeras palabras vienen en el mismo comunicado oficial del anuncio y que traducimos a continuación: Hay que leer estas palabras con lupa porque están escritas y medidas al milímetro . Cuando el cofundador de Nvidia habla de «humildad» y «compromiso renovado» y agradece la «deliberación» del consejo, está claro que lo que quiere es pedir una tregua pública tras once días de auténtico vértigo: desde su dimisión el pasado 12 de noviembre hasta el giro de 180 grados de una junta directiva que, apenas unos días antes, había descartado tajantemente su regreso. El subtexto es evidente: Huang asume de forma velada el desgaste reputacional de un escándalo personal que llegó a castigar la cotización de la compañía, pero al mismo tiempo vuelve desde una posición de fuerza tras quedar demostrado que ni los inversores, ni la plantilla, ni siquiera la Casa Blanca (no olvidemos el respaldo público de Donald Trump) concebían una Nvidia sin su arquitecto al timón. Esa misma lectura estratégica explica el reparto de agradecimientos con el que busca pasar página y blindar el futuro inmediato de la empresa . Al elogiar explícitamente el liderazgo de Harvey Jones al frente del consejo y el papel de Colette Kress como consejera delegada interina, Huang proyecta normalidad institucional y desactiva cualquier sospecha de fractura interna, justo mientras Nvidia mantiene abierta la investigación independiente y crea un nuevo puesto de director de cumplimiento normativo para disipar las dudas sobre seguridad nacional en Washington. Llama también la atención su mención expresa al apoyo de su familia , que funciona como una especie de cortafuegos para dar por zanjada la dimensión personal de la polémica (quizá como recordatorio a su yo del futuro), mientras que su apelación a liderar «una nueva revolución industrial» devuelve el foco al único terreno donde su figura resulta insustituible: el despliegue global de la infraestructura de inteligencia artificial, un argumento que Wall Street ha comprado de inmediato celebrando su vuelta con fuertes subidas antes de la apertura del mercado. En Xataka | Nvidia es el Super Glue de la industria de la IA. Sin Huang al frente, temen que sea pegamento de barra

sources.name: Computer Hoy
sources.title: Nvidia recupera a Jensen Huang como CEO tras semanas de incertidumbre y las acciones se disparan
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. ¡Las acciones se disparan, Wall Street reacciona y persisten dudas sobre la compañía! Nvidia restituye a Jensen Huang como CEO tras once días de incertidumbre. Tras confesar la infidelidad junto al caso de espionaje y ser investigado por posibles filtraciones de secretos empresariales , Jensen Hueng fue revocado de su puesto y los nombres que sonaban con fuerza para el reemplazo eran Tim Cook o Eric Schmidt , pero eso parece que ya se terminó. A pesar de la crisis de liderazgo por la que ha estado pasando el exCEO de Nvidia durante las últimas semanas, las cosas están cambiando drásticamente porque el consejo de administración ha decidido restituir al cofundador de la gran compañía que lidera el mercado de las tarjetas gráficas con la RTX 5090 . La decisión parece llegar justo tras una fuerte presión política, dudas sobre el futuro de la marca y el impacto financiero que ha significado el cambio. Sí, el regreso de Jensen Huang está aquí , aunque el peso de su trabajo como jefe, después de los recientes inconvenientes, podría ser incluso más diferente de lo esperado. ¿ Quieres saber qué va a pasar con la próxima serie de las GPUs ? Puede que te interese todo lo relacionado con este caso porque también ha hecho que las acciones se disparen. ¿Huang está de regreso y Nvidia no requiere de otro CEO? ¿Qué está pasando con toda la compañía? Se desata una nueva oleada de noticias alrededor de este acontecimiento porque en un principio se pensaba que ya era más que evidente que ya no formaría parte del equipo después de estar por más de tres décadas. Pues bien, la junta directiva de Nvidia ha aprobado por unanimidad la restitución de Jensen Huang como director ejecutivo después de que la compañía asegurase haber consultado la decisión con "altos niveles" de la administración estadounidense. Tras ser categorizado como alguien sospechoso por ser infiel a su esposa con una espía china, la investigación ha dado como conclusión que la empresa considera que no existe un riesgo para la seguridad nacional que justifique apartar definitivamente a su fundador. Esto termina inclinando la balanza a favor de su regreso. Harvey Jones, presidente del consejo, defendió la decisión afirmando lo siguiente: Apenas se conoció la noticia, las acciones de Nvidia llegaron a dispararse más de un 30 % en las operaciones previas a la apertura de Wall Street. Según los datos difundidos tras el anuncio, la valoración bursátil de la compañía pasó de situarse ligeramente por encima de los 3 billones de dólares a superar los 4 billones en cuestión de minutos (aproximadamente 3,67 billones de euros), un salto que pone de manifiesto la enorme confianza que todavía genera el ejecutivo entre accionistas. El propio Huang no tardó en pronunciarse después de hacerse oficial su regreso. "No puedo esperar para volver al trabajo" , declaró el directivo. A la celebración también se sumó Donald Trump, quien defendió públicamente la reincorporación del empresario y aseguró que Estados Unidos necesita su liderazgo para mantener la competitividad tecnológica del país. La estrecha relación entre ambos había sido objeto de especulación durante los días previos, especialmente tras aparecer informaciones que vinculaban al fundador de Nvidia con varias investigaciones e interrogantes relacionados con operaciones comerciales internacionales, se indica en NVIDIA Newsroom . Aunque la restitución de Jensen Huang reduce la incertidumbre inmediata sobre el liderazgo de Nvidia, el movimiento está lejos de cerrar todas las preguntas que han surgido durante esta crisis . De hecho, la situación ha servido para mostrar hasta qué punto la compañía depende de su fundador. Diversas informaciones apuntan a que decenas de directivos reportan directamente al CEO y que Huang participa de forma activa en decisiones estratégicas que van desde acuerdos comerciales hasta inversiones y relaciones con clientes clave del negocio de la inteligencia artificial. Uno de los aspectos que más interés genera entre analistas e inversores es el denominado "círculo" financiero atribuido a Nvidia. El resultado era una red de operaciones que alimentaba la demanda de hardware. La entonces CEO interina y directora financiera, Colette Kress, habría planteado una revisión más estricta de estos mecanismos por considerar que algunos procesos necesitaban una mayor separación entre inversión estratégica y actividad comercial. Siguen existiendo dudas sobre determinadas operaciones internacionales relacionadas con el suministro de chips. Tampoco desaparecen los interrogantes sobre el modelo de crecimiento que ha impulsado a Nvidia hasta convertirse en una de las compañías más valiosas del planeta.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: SpaceX sued by Oregon and Virginia over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims
sources.text: Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator. Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled users to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation , the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others. In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material. The complaints also allege that SpaceX has falsely represented its AI apps and social network (Grok and X) as generally safe, which the states see as a violation of Virginia's Consumer Protection Act or Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The matter is particularly concerning because X allows minors 13 and older to access its content. Rayfield and Jones both noted in their complaints that harms caused by non-consensual, sexualized images go beyond the victims depicted in the images. "This content can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content," Jones wrote. Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes important norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation." In a statement emailed to CNBC by a spokesperson for SpaceXSI, and posted on the company's @Safety account on X, the company said, "When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement. Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors." At an NYC Council hearing in October , a SpaceX AI policy leader, Gabriela Castillo Madrid, said the company had appropriate "safeguards" and "strict controls" in place around its AI products. SpaceX was already facing multiple Grok- and X-related lawsuits, and government probes around the world, including by authorities in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and the state of California. In private-sector lawsuits filed against SpaceX in the U.S. concerning Grok and AI-generated, explicit images, litigation is still in early stages and is tracked by The Center for Internet Technology Addiction. When the city of Baltimore sued xAI, now owned and operated by SpaceX, the company argued that under Section 230, they were not liable for unwanted images. Section 230 is a federal law that largely shields online platforms from liability for users' content. SpaceX also sued a user in a federal court in the Northern District of Texas for breach of contract after he allegedly used Grok to create and distribute deepfake explicit images, including depictions of minors. Lawyers for Musk's company argued that Grok should be seen as "a neutral tool, subject to user control," and that any image generation "is the result of the user's prompts and directions." The new state suits add to legal pressure on SpaceX. Both Virginia and Oregon are seeking injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs, while Virginia is also seeking restitution for consumers from Musk's company. Oregon submitted its complaint to the Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening, and Virginia submitted its complaint to the City of Richmond Circuit Court Monday morning . As of early Monday, the suits were pending the courts' acceptance. State attorneys general have recently succeeded in compelling U.S. social media companies to change their products and pay for alleged past harms. In August, for example, Meta settled a major federal case centered on allegations that the social media giant misrepresented the level of child mental health problems caused by its apps, Facebook and Instagram . Without admitting to wrongdoing, Meta agreed to pay states around $17 billion over a 10-year period and to make app changes that experts believe will help keep children safer online.

sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
sources.text: State AGs called the weak safeguards built into Elon Musk’s AI image generator ‘not a failure but a feature.’﻿ State AGs called the weak safeguards built into Elon Musk’s AI image generator ‘not a failure but a feature.’﻿ In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and “instead saw a market opportunity for more profits,” describing the weak safeguards around Grok as “not a failure but a feature.” “Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” Jones said in a press statement . “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation.” The complaints largely center around Grok Imagine, a tool that allows Grok and X users to generate images and videos. In August 2025, Grok maker xAI (which Musk has since merged with SpaceX ) launched a “spicy” mode for Grok Imagine that spat out sexualized content including nude deepfakes of celebrities like Taylor Swift. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature that allowed X users to instantly edit any image without requiring consent from the original poster — resulting in X becoming flooded with nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes of adults and minors . xAI made several changes to restrict access to Grok image editing, moving some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear, or explicit scenarios. Our testing at the Verge following these restriction updates found they did little to prevent the bot from creating sexualized deepfakes, however. Both of the Oregon and Virginia lawsuits are seeking financial damages. The X Safety team said in a statement released after the lawsuits were announced that it takes appropriate measures to address users who generate sexual content involving minors: “The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards. When some of these bad actors found ways to misuse Grok Imagine earlier this year, we acted promptly to tighten its protections, which are designed to refuse any request to generate explicit images of minors or real people. To stay ahead of this disgusting and indefensible conduct, we keep testing and adjusting those protections as these abusers change tactics. We also implement sophisticated classifiers that screen every prompt before an image is generated and check every output after.”

sources.text: Get more helpful Search responses by securely opting in to connect Google Wallet, Drive, and the Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode. This helps you track financial goals, organize project information, and continue research tasks without repeating yourself. You remain in control and can manage these connections in your settings at any time. So if you’ve been researching and planning for a trip, you can pick up right where you left off in a new search thread without starting over or repeating yourself. As always, you can adjust or turn off personalization at any time in your Search Settings. Sign up for our newsletters with product updates, event information, special offers, and more. You may opt out at any time.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
sources.text: Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos. By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time. Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money. As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season. Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa. Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses. The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context. sources.title: Trump ha movido ficha para recuperar a Jensen Huang en Nvidia: su relación con el fundador va mucho más allá de la tecnología
sources.text: El pasado 12 de noviembre, Jensen Huang dimitía como CEO de Nvidia, hundido por un truculento escándalo en el que se mezclaban infidelidades, geopolítica y sospechas de espionaje para China. Once días después, el mismo consejo que aceptó su salida lo ha vuelto a readmitir como CEO por unanimidad. Entre una fecha y otra, hubo una mano que no dejó de presionar a Nvidia para que Huang " volviera al trabajo ": Donald Trump. La readmisión de Huang resuelve un gigantesco problema sucesorio para Nvidia, pero arroja una duda sobre la compañía: ¿hasta qué punto es independiente Nvidia de las decisiones que se toman en el despacho oval? Una amistad con contraprestaciones . Según contaba NBC , el vínculo entre Huang y Donald Trump nació en una cena en Mar-a-Lago. Esa confianza fue creciendo hasta el punto de que, tal y como Huang reconoció en una entrevista con AP , el presidente "me llama en mitad de la noche y quiere hablar de alguno de estos temas". Huang ha pisado la Casa Blanca nueve veces y en septiembre se sentó en la mesa principal de una cena de Estado, junto a Trump y Xi Jinping. También acompañó al presidente en su viaje oficial a China en mayo, donde incluso se desvió el plan de vuelo del Air Force One para recoger a Huang en Alaska. La Administración le devolvió el favor al suavizar restricciones de Biden, lo que permitió vender sus chips de la generación anterior a China. Huang defendía que era más seguro enganchar a las empresas chinas a la tecnología de EEUU que empujarlas a buscar otra . Dinero y altavoz para la IA . Por su parte, Nvidia ha financiado con mucho dinero las iniciativas de Trump. La tecnológica aportó 25 millones de dólares al salón de baile de la Casa Blanca situándose como una de las principales donantes, solo empatada con Apple y la familia Adelson. Su gasto en lobby se ha multiplicado por ocho en este mandato y superó los 2,5 millones en el tercer trimestre, según los registros públicos que cita NBC. En pleno evento All-In, Trump le llamó mientras todavía estaba en el escenario y Huang pidió un micro para que todos oyeran al presidente tachar de "engaño" la petición de frenar la IA. Su respuesta: "Tiene usted razón. No vamos a permitir que eso suceda, señor". Lo que calló es que si la IA se ralentiza, caen los pedidos de chips, y esos chips los fabrica Nvidia. Una mano frota a la otra. Esa espía de la que usted me habla. Alice Huang, exdirectiva de Megaspeed, estaba siendo investigada por desviar chips a China algunos meses antes de que se hiciera público su affair con Huang. Según el NYT, Washington la vigilaba desde hacía un año. Pekín niega su implicación en el caso de espionaje. Trump, sin embargo, restó peso al asunto. Dijo que no sabía si era espía, a pesar de los avisos de sus propios servicios, y afirmó : "Si la mujer era una espía, sí. Si no lo era, quizás sería diferente". Ante los periodistas añadió que a cualquier mujer hermosa que llega de China "dicen que es una espía". El Gobierno que la vigilaba tan de cerca como para conocer qué relación mantenía con Huang es el que ahora da por buena la vuelta de Huang. Un consejo que da marcha atrás . El lunes 16 Trump dijo que " no le importaría " ver de vuelta a Huang al frente de Nvidia. El domingo escribió en su red social Truth que readmitirlo "sería lo mejor para la empresa y también para Estados Unidos". Una recogida de firmas con más de 206.000 participantes, entre ellos figuras como Elon Musk, también presionaba para que el consejo oyera las peticiones de readmisión de Huang. Harvey Jones, presidente del consejo, había dicho apenas seis días antes que no había intención de restituirlo . Ya se advertía de que hacerlo parecería obedecer a la Casa Blanca. Pero ha pasado. La llamada del presidente . En su comunicado, el consejo de administración de Nvidia asegura que recibió información de altos cargos del Gobierno de EEUU y que, con ella, la vuelta de Huang no es un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. Lo que Nvidia no cuenta en su comunicado es que también recibió la llamada de Trump presionando a su junta directiva para que Huang recuperara su puesto, tal y como desvela Semafor . Trump celebró que la junta "ha tomado la decisión correcta y adecuada", y las acciones de la compañía se dispararon hasta subir más del 31% antes de la apertura. Nvidia no es una empresa estatal, pero el calendario sugiere quién marcó el ritmo para que Huang volviera a ser su CEO. En Xataka | Nvidia no ha despedido a Jensen Huang: ha aceptado su dimisión, y esa diferencia abre la puerta a su vuelta

sources.title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
sources.text: Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.﻿ Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.﻿ After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO , following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director. “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC . Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air. Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times , so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday. News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility. Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration. The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report , as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st. The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation. The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added. Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times , which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the
